title: Synthesis harness for mixed-tenancy batching + queueing effects
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Goal: Build and run a deterministic yet stochastic-parameterized harness that synthesizes mixed-tenant traffic (short chat sessions, long completion sessions, embeddings bursts) to isolate how continuous batching interacts with queueing/backpressure and KV-cache amplification.

Hypotheses: 1) A small fraction of long sessions combined with bursty short sessions will amplify p95 tail via head-of-line queueing even when median throughput is stable. 2) KV-cache hits materially change effective tokens/sec under batching by reducing token generation time variance, thereby altering optimal batch-window tuning. 3) Client-side pacing interacts with the runtime's continuous batching window to create non-linear throughput cliffs under certain arrival skews.

What this ticket produces: a reusable harness (stochastic session mixer) + measurement suite that reports per-tenant and global metrics: tokens/sec (instant + 1m avg), per-session p50/p95/p99 latency, queue depth histogram, batch size distribution, KV-cache hit rate, and change-point annotations. The harness will include injected network jitter and simulated tenant priority classes to validate routing/fallback behaviors.

Workplan:
- Design traffic mixer with parameters: short:long ratio, burstiness (CV), arrival autocorrelation (rho), client pacing jitter, tenant weight distribution.
- Implement runtime-side probes to capture batch composition and KV cache tag per request.
- Add streaming exporter that logs events to an S3-compatible test bucket and a local InfluxDB instance for plotting.
- Implement regression detection rules: CUSUM-based change detection on p95 and a tokens/sec drop threshold with at least 3 sigma deviation sustained for 1 minute.
- Run grid sweep across parameter space and produce summary surface: p95 vs short:long ratio vs median batch wait time.

Acceptance criteria:
- Harness can reproduce at least two deterministic failure modes documented in doc (head-of-line p95 spike, kv-hit-induced throughput cliff).
- Regression detector emits a signal when p95 increases by >25% sustained for 60s with fewer than 5 false positives in baseline runs.
- Output artifacts: confluence doc with run methodology, GitHub PR implementing harness, dashboard with interactive heatmaps.

Artifacts/links:
- Confluence draft: https://redwood.atlassian.net/l/cp/synth-batch-queueing-harness (internal)
- Initial PR (WIP): https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2486
- Dashboard (test cluster): https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/bench/mixed-tenancy-batch-queueing

Notes on trade-offs: We intentionally keep per-request instrumentation lightweight (only a few tags) to avoid perturbing microsecond-level latency. For deeper traces we will toggle higher-overhead modes for small-scale experiments. We accept that synthetic traffic cannot perfectly emulate all customer workloads; emphasis is on spanning corner-case parameter regimes that historically caused regressions in CI.
